1. Heard Mr. Raghvendra Pradhan, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. S.S.
Baghel, PL for the respondents /State.
2.

The petitioner has preferred this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 219/2023 registered at police of Police Station Rakhi, District Raipur for commission of offence punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of the IPC.

3. Facts of the case are that one person impersonating himself to be Akash Jain alongwith identification i.e. Adhaar Card etc. stated that he is power of attorney holder of Kamlesh Jain and shown his original registered power of attorney.

The petitioner after going through the aforesaid document entered into an agreement to sell an agricultural land situated at Village Tandul, P.H. No.
26, R.I. Circle Paloud, Tahsil Mandir Hasaud, District Raipur (C.G.) with said person, who stated that the said land is of ownership of Kamlesh Jain and he is Akash Jain, who is power of attorney holder of said Kamlesh Jain and he shown the said agricultural land to the petitioner for the purpose of selling and the petitioner agreed to purchase the said land after getting the information from the revenue authorities about the ownership of said land.

Further, it was agreed between the parties,
that the petitioner will purchase the said land for a total amount of Rs.2 crores and as agreed between the parties and the sale-deed was registered.

It is pertinent to mention here that after getting the sale deed executed in favour of the petitioner, the next date i.e. 22-12-2023 was Friday and 23.12.2023 was Saturday, on which date the bank was closed and on 24.12.2013 was Sunday and on 25.12.2023 was Christmas, on account of which the Banks were closed and in between the petitioner came to know that the person, who sold the land to him by stating himself as Akash jain and shown himself as power of attorney of Kamlesh Jain, was a forged person, thereafter, he approached the concerned police station for making FIR against the said person and when the police denied to receive the complaint of petitioner, he sent the same through Speed Post and then he also made complaint to the Superintendent of Police, Raipur on 26.12.2023.

4. It is surprising for the petitioner that one person namely Lakhan Killekar has made complaint on the same date i.e. 26.12.2023 in respect of the forged registration of the sale-deed in respect of property of Smt. Kamlesh Jain and he showed himself as the employee of Smt. Kamlesh Jain, as a consequence, police registered his FIR bearing Crime No. 219 / 2023 under Sections 120-B, 420,
467, 468 & 471 of the IPC and the police authorities, without taking into consideration that the Anwar Alam vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63443645/

sentences.text: 2 petitioner has also made complaint of forgery, which has been committed against him, has added the name of the petitioner as co-accused in the the said FIR, whereas, according to the petitioner, he was actually victim of the said forgery.
In pursuance thereof, the petitioner was got arrested and the learned Sessions Court after taking into consideration the case of the petitioner has granted regular bail after some days of his arrest.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner vehemently argued that the petitioner happens to be a bonafide purchaser of the property in question and he purchased the same by paying Rs. 2 crores and his arrest was also made in a very suspicious manner and he is sent to jail and subsequently, he has been granted regular bail and there appears to be no evidence collected against the petitioner during course of investigation, as such, the FIR lodged against the petitioner is liable to be set aside / quashed.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer made by counsel for the petitioner for quashment of the FIR and submits that statement of the complainant as well as the original land owner Kamlesh Jain has already been recorded, further investigation is still pending and the private land was purchased by the petitioner by paying Rs.2 crores, but it was much less than the market rate, therefore, the petition is liable to be dismissed.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, having regard to the facts & circumstances of the case, particularly, considering the fact that matter is still under investigation, the statement of original land owner has been recorded by police and the land shown to be purchased by showing payment of 2 Crores which is much less than the market value.
We are not inclined to entertain this petition at this stage.
However, the Investigating Officer is directed to complete the investigation and submit a police report under Section 173(2) of Cr.P.C. if any, expeditiously.
8. With the aforesaid observations & directions, the writ petition stands finally disposed of.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Bibhu Datta Guru ) (Ramesh Sinha)
